title: pi-ui core vocabulary
description: Identifiers, versions and errors shared by the whole pi-ui wire surface (REST /api/v1, WebSocket /ws/v1, pi child protocol). Self-contained on purpose: server/scripts/gen.sh generates one Go file per schemas/*.json, so a cross-file $ref would produce code that does not compile. Objects are lenient: additionalProperties defaults to true and is never written out, so unknown fields survive a round trip and the generated Go types stay dependency-free.

ServerSessionId.description: Server-assigned session id: "s_" plus 16 lowercase hex characters drawn from crypto/rand. Never derived from the cwd or the session name.

DeviceId.description: Opaque device identifier minted by the server at pairing time. The minting format belongs to the pairing implementation, so clients must treat the value as opaque and never parse it.

TerminalId.description: Opaque identifier of one server-owned PTY terminal. Scoped to a session; never interpreted by the client.

TaskId.description: Opaque identifier of one server-owned background task (long command, job wrapper).

JobId.description: Opaque identifier of one long-running server job such as an update or index run.

RequestId.description: Correlation id of one request/response pair: a REST request, a WS command ("c1"), an extension UI dialog or a replay cursor.

EntryId.description: pi session entry id, copied verbatim from the child's entry_appended records (payload.entry.id). Never generated or rewritten by the server.

Seq.description: Monotonic per-session event sequence number assigned by the WS hub. Replay cursors are expressed in Seq values.

Timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp. The server emits UTC with milliseconds when the publisher leaves it empty. Expressed as a pattern instead of "format": "date-time" so codegen keeps it a string; a time.Time alias would not round-trip as text on the wire.

ProtocolVersion.description: Wire protocol version. Negotiated in the WS hello/welcome frames and echoed in the X-Piui-Protocol header. A future v2 ships alongside v1 (dual support) instead of changing v1 shapes.

Scope.description: Authorization scope of an authenticated client: viewer reads, operator drives sessions, admin manages the server itself.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error taxonomy. Clients switch on these values, so they are never renamed or reused; new failures get a new code and unknown codes must degrade to a generic message. `feature_disabled` is the server's own policy: an administrative setting turned the capability off (for example `git.write`), which is different from the caller's scope not covering it.

message.description: Human-readable English message, safe to display: no provider secrets, no paths outside the session cwd, no conversation content.

details.description: Optional structured context (sessionId, limit, retryAfterMs, field, ...). Open map so a new detail never breaks a client; clients ignore unknown keys.

ApiError.description: Error body of every REST failure ({"error": {...}}) and of the WS response.error / server.error frames. Unknown sibling fields are allowed and preserved.

version.description: pi-ui server version, e.g. "0.0.1-spike" (stamped into the binary at build time).

piVersion.description: pi version the server was built and probed against (0.87.1 in the spike). A mismatch degrades with a clear message instead of failing mid-run.

features.description: Capability flags the server advertises ("terminal", "git", "mcp", ...). Clients degrade gracefully when a flag is missing and ignore flags they do not know.

limits.description: Server limits as scalars (maxSessions, replayEvents, replayWindowSec, dialogTimeoutSec, heartbeatSec, ...). Open map so a new limit lands without a breaking schema change.

ServerInfo.description: Body of GET /api/v1/server and of the server field inside the WS welcome frame.
